evidence.quote: A novel Co-Ni-Ti-V-based superalloy exhibiting low density and high strength
The images presented in Fig. 6 (a)-(f) reveal the EPMA images of six distinct alloys: 10Ni-2V, 15Ni-2V, 20Ni-2V, 10Ni-4V, 15Ni-4V, and 20Ni-4V.
a sequence of Co-20Ni-10Ti-4V-xAl alloys (where x = 1, 3, or 6 denotes 1Al, 3Al, and 6Al, respectively) has been devised.

Utilizing CALPHAD method, a Co-20Ni-10Ti-4V quaternary superalloy with excellent properties has been designed, exhibiting high value of yield strength (after 48 h of annealing at 750 degC, 1358 Mpa at room temperature & 512 Mpa at 900 degC).
With increasing Ni and V contents, the gamma prime solvus temperature increased and the gamma / gamma prime lattice mismatch decreased in the Co-xNi-10Ti-yV (x = 10, 15 and 20; y = 2 and 4) alloys.

The Co-20Ni-10Ti-4V-1Al alloy developed in this study has high gamma prime solvus temperature (~1220.7 degC), low density (~8.15 g/cm3), low gamma / gamma prime lattice mismatch (~0.67%), excellent gamma prime phase thermal stability, and low gamma prime precipitates coarsening rate (~1.940 x 10 28 m3/s at 750 degC).

To prepare button ingots of approximately 30 g, cobalt, titanium, nickel, vanadium, and chromium (with a purity of at least 99.99 wt%) were melted using an arc melting unit under high-purity Ar atmosphere.
To encourage atomic diffusion, the samples were cold-rolled at a reduction rate of 60% before equilibration treatment at low temperatures.
The samples were first solution treated at 1200 – 1250 °C for 24 – 48 h, followed by annealing at 750 – 1000 °C.
